study type: Difference-in-differences evaluation using repeated cross-sectional data
exposure: Removal of user fees for facility-based delivery services
outcome: Proportion of births delivered in facilities
Proportion of births delivered by caesarean section
cohort: The study involved births occurring in ten sub-Saharan African countries, captured by Demographic and Health Surveys between 1997 and 2012.
finding: The removal of user fees was associated with an increase of 3.1 facility-based deliveries per 100 live births and an estimated reduction of 2.9 neonatal deaths per 1000 births.
mod_finding: There was no evidence of an increase in caesarean deliveries following the policy change.
country: Ten sub-Saharan African countries (Kenya, Ghana, Senegal, and seven unspecified others)
cross-section timing: Data collected from Demographic and Health Surveys between 1997 and 2012.
